Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def transform(grid):
    # Overlay the marker locations in the top sparse field onto the lower field.
    # Keep the lower field's fill color and highlight simultaneous marks.
    sep = next(i for i, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1)
    top, bottom = grid[:sep], grid[sep + 1:]
    return [[3 if a != grid[0][0] and b != grid[-1][0] else grid[-1][0]
             for a, b in zip(ra, rb)] for ra, rb in zip(top, bottom)]

def transform(grid):
    # Two same-sized panels separated by a solid divider; keep cells blank in both.
    sep = next(i for i, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1)
    if sep == 0 or sep == len(grid)-1:
        a, b = grid[:sep], grid[sep+1:]
        bg_a = max(set(v for row in a for v in row), key=lambda v: sum(r.count(v) for r in a))
        bg_b = max(set(v for row in b for v in row), key=lambda v: sum(r.count(v) for r in b))
        return [[3 if x == bg_a and y == bg_b else 9 for x,y in zip(ra,rb)] for ra,rb in zip(a,b)]
    # Vertical divider
    left=[row[:sep] for row in grid]; right=[row[sep+1:] for row in grid]
    bg_a=max(set(v for row in left for v in row),key=lambda v:sum(r.count(v) for r in left))
    bg_b=max(set(v for row in right for v in row),key=lambda v:sum(r.count(v) for r in right))
    return [[3 if x==bg_a and y==bg_b else 9 for x,y in zip(ra,rb)] for ra,rb in zip(left,right)]

def transform(grid):
    # Align the two square panels around a uniform separator; output their
    # overlapping background cells as 3 and all other positions as 9.
    sep = next((i for i, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1), None)
    if sep is not None:
        a, b = grid[:sep], grid[sep+1:]
        bg_a = max(set(v for r in a for v in r), key=lambda v: sum(r.count(v) for r in a))
        bg_b = max(set(v for r in b for v in r), key=lambda v: sum(r.count(v) for r in b))
        return [[3 if x == bg_a and y == bg_b else 9 for x,y in zip(ra,rb)] for ra,rb in zip(a,b)]
    sep = next(i for i in range(len(grid[0])) if len({r[i] for r in grid}) == 1)
    a=[r[:sep] for r in grid]; b=[r[sep+1:] for r in grid]
    # Uniform side field can include unused padding; align equal-sized panels.
    width=min(len(a[0]),len(b[0]))
    a=[r[-width:] for r in a]; b=[r[:width] for r in b]
    bg_a=max(set(v for r in a for v in r),key=lambda v:sum(r.count(v) for r in a))
    bg_b=max(set(v for r in b for v in r),key=lambda v:sum(r.count(v) for r in b))
    return [[3 if x==bg_a and y==bg_b else 9 for x,y in zip(ra,rb)] for ra,rb in zip(a,b)]
